chunks: Muhammad ibn 'Abdillah ibn Ja'far Al-Himyari narrated to me from his father, from someone who narrated to him, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hashim, from Dawud ibn Farqad, from Abi Hamzah, from Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
An obligatory prayer in the Mosque of Kufah is equal to an accepted Hajj, and a recommended prayer in it is equal to an accepted 'Umrah.
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for praying in the Mosque of Kufah according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Kamil al-Ziyarat*, Ibn Qulawayh records this tradition from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to highlight the spiritual potency of the Mosque of Kufah, a site deeply associated with the Ahl al-Bayt and early Islamic history. The comparison of a single obligatory prayer to a full Hajj and a voluntary prayer to an Umrah underscores the unique sanctity of this location in Shia devotional practice, often linked to the martyrdom of Imam Ali (AS) and the presence of his shrine.
